Part 2 · Worksheet and risk

How does one deviation become a ranked row?

Part 2 · the plan

From a guide word to a rank

  1. Guide wordseleven prompts on each parameter
  2. One worked rowN1, header pressure falls, column by column
  3. Severity and likelihoodS without safeguards, L with them
  4. The matrixR = S × L in four bands
  5. Safeguardswhat the plant already has

Interactive · parameter and guide word

Parameter plus guide word gives a deviation

A guide word is a prompt, not an answer: the team keeps only deviations with a credible cause.

PHA Studio · step 3 · worked example N1

One row, as the scribe records it

N1.1 Pressure / LESS; the green ▶ OTS 1 chip means the simulator can run a cause

Next, the same row one column at a time.

Interactive · step through the columns

Deviation, causes, consequences, safeguards, rank

Consequences are written as if no safeguard worked; only then are safeguards listed.

Interactive · pick a level

S judges the harm; L judges how often, with safeguards

The worked row: flaring for hours is S2; happened on similar platforms is L3.

Interactive · click a cell

R = S × L falls in one of four bands

Risk rank$R=S\times L$

The worked row sits at S2, L3: R 6, Medium, so an owner and a due date.

Interactive · pick a type

99 safeguards already loaded from this OTS

Alarms and trips dominate; each must be checked against what it really does.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Parameter plus guide word gives the deviation.
  • Consequences first, with no credit for safeguards.
  • S without safeguards, L with them; R = S × L.
  • The worked row ranks Medium: R 6.

Part 3 · Test, act, report

Is the row right, and who closes it?

Part 3 · the plan

From a row to evidence and actions

  1. ▶ OTSwhich deviations the simulator can run
  2. The testlined out, then the cause, hands off
  3. The evidencealarms, trip, key tags
  4. Back to the rowdid each safeguard act?
  5. Close-outdata check, report, workshop

Interactive · pick a node

27 causes the simulator can run, in ten nodes

A test checks one cause of the row; the others are judged from the drawings.

From the row to the console

Lined out, one cause, no hands on the controls

▶ OTS on the worked row offers test T04

  • K-100 starts at design.
  • The cause starts at $T_0$ = 60 s.
  • Controllers named by the test are held in manual (MAN).
  • Only the existing safeguards act.

Interactive · drag the clock · model run, noise off

PV-102 passing: the flare rises, export falls, no trip

The FI-109 alarm sounds at 1:14; the flared gas is lost from export.

Above the DCS · after 20 min

The panel writes the evidence for the Notes cell

So the row now carries evidence, not only the team's opinion.

Interactive · pick a claim of the row

Did each safeguard act, and was the consequence right?

Only the alarm acted; the test supports S2 and the recommendation to test the seat.

Interactive · fill or empty the row

The data check finds what the meeting forgot

Errors block the report; a High row needs a recommendation or a LOPA.

PHA Studio · workshop mode and step 6

Run the meeting on the projector, then report

Workshop mode: node, parameter, guide word, timer

  • Timer per node: 5 to 30 min.
  • Ideas from phones by a scanned code (QR).
  • Report: print, Word, HTML; workbook in Excel.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • 27 causes in ten nodes can be run on the simulator.
  • A test starts at design, hands off, cause at 60 s.
  • T04: alarm at 1:14, 20 t/h to flare, no trip.
  • The data check gates the report.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Read each node's intent before applying a guide word.

2

Write consequences as if no safeguard worked.

3

Rank with R = S × L and act on the band.

4

Test a row on the simulator and paste the evidence.

5

Clear the data check before the report goes out.
